about:
# GroupHighlight

Put an arrow above your party and raid members, so you can find them in a crowd. One arrow per player, in their class colour or a colour you pick.

[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/curseforge/v/1798373?label=CurseForge)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/group-highlight) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/curseforge/dt/1798373?label=downloads)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/group-highlight) [![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight?label=GitHub)](https://github.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/releases/latest)

## Usage

### Editor

![Editor: a header band with the logo, and boxes for who gets an arrow, the look, a preview and party colours, with the amber warning at the bottom.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/master/docs/images/1-editor.png)

- `/gh` or `/grouphighlight`: open the editor. Type it again (or press Esc) to close it.
- Drag the header band (with the logo and the name) to move the window. Everything you change shows up in the game world immediately, and the position of the window is kept.
- The editor has four boxes: **Who gets an arrow**, **Look**, **Preview** and **Party colours**. Hover over any option for a tooltip.
- **Who gets an arrow**: Off, Party (everyone in your party except yourself) or Party + Raid. **Also above yourself** and **Also above your target** are separate switches.
- **Reset**: the boxes Who gets an arrow, Look and Party colours have a small reset icon next to their title that puts only that box back to its defaults. Click it twice: the first click shows **Click again** in red for three seconds.
- The amber band at the bottom says that arrows don't work above friendly players inside dungeons and raids.
- Close the window with the cross in the header band.

### Window size

- Drag the grip in the bottom right corner to change the width and height of the window (it can't be made wider than the default). The size is kept.
- Wide, the boxes sit in two columns; narrow, in one column. When the boxes don't fit, a thin scroll bar appears.
- Right-click the grip to go back to the default size.

### Look

![Look: a triangle (filled or outline) or one, two or three chevrons, with or without fading out.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/master/docs/images/2-look.png)

- A triangle (filled or outline) or one, two or three chevrons (with or without fading out).
- **Arrow size** and **Lift above name** set how big the arrow is and how high it sits. The preview shows the result.

### Party colours

![Party colours: a table with a name and a colour swatch per group member.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/master/docs/images/3-party-colours.png)

- Arrows use the class colour by default.
- The table lists your party (in a raid: everyone in the raid), with yourself only when **Also above yourself** is on. With more than five names it scrolls.
- Left-click a swatch to open the colour picker for that player, right-click to go back to the class colour.
- A chosen colour is remembered by name and realm.

### Colour picker

![Colour picker: the colour and its hex code at the top, a colour field, a hue bar, presets, and Cancel and Okay.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/master/docs/images/4-colour-picker.png)

- The picker is fixed to the editor, next to it at the height of the Party colours table, and moves with it.
- It has a colour field, a hue bar and a preset for every class. The new colour and its hex code are in its title bar; type six hex digits there, for example FF8800. The result shows in the game immediately.
- **Okay** keeps the colour, **Cancel** or Esc puts the old one back.
- Choosing exactly the class colour stores nothing, so the player keeps following their class.

### Key binding

- Settings > Keybindings > AddOns > GroupHighlight has **Turn the arrows on or off**. Bind a key to it yourself.
- Pressing it sets the mode to Off. Pressing it again brings back the mode you had before, for example Party + Raid, and not the default mode. The other options stay as they are.
- Each press shows the new mode in a toast at the top of the screen, for example "Highlight: Off.". Click a toast to close it.

### Settings panel

- Settings > AddOns > GroupHighlight has an **Open GroupHighlight** button that opens the editor (or type `/gh`).

### Limitations

- **Arrows need nameplates.** An arrow only appears above a unit that has a visible nameplate. Units without one (objects, units out of nameplate range or out of view) get no arrow.
- **Friendly nameplates.** Only the party and raid modes change nameplate settings: while one is active, the `nameplateShowFriends`, `nameplateShowFriendlyPlayers` and `nameplateShowAll` CVars are turned on, and your previous values are restored when you select Off. CVar changes wait until combat ends.
- **Dungeons and raids.** The game blocks addons from friendly nameplates there, so arrows above other players cannot be shown. Friendly nameplates are therefore not turned on inside dungeons, raids and scenarios: your own setting comes back on entering and the addon's again on leaving. Raid markers are no alternative: placing them is a protected action that addons are not allowed to do.
- **Your target.** Works for players and enemies, and for friendly NPCs when you have friendly NPC nameplates turned on in the game's nameplate settings. The target option never changes your nameplate settings, and its tooltip shows which case applies.
- **Yourself.** You have no nameplate, and addons cannot read the screen position of a character, so the arrow above yourself sits at a fixed spot above the screen centre and scales with the camera zoom.

## Development

Please see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for development checks and contribution guidance.

## Feedback

Please remember that I'm always working to improve the addon, so I'm interested in hearing directly from you about anything you want to share or ask. You can report this using the issues on GitHub.
When reporting bugs or unexpected behavior, include your addon version and an overview of your current options.

## Changelog

Please see the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for more information about recent changes.

releases.notes:
### Fixed
- Header text stays inside the window and ends with. ([18aad77](https://github.com/jordinbrouwer/GroupHighlight/commit/18aad77359d1dbb0c282031e0ff250b429854082))

### Added
- The editor can be resized: drag the grip in the bottom right corner to change its width and height, right-click it to go back to the default size. Wide, the sections sit in two columns; narrow, in one column with a thin scroll bar.
- In a raid, Party colours lists everyone in the raid. With more than five names the list scrolls.
- A hint "or type /gh" under the button on the settings page.

### Changed
- New look for the editor, the colour picker and the settings page in GroupHighlight's own gold and grey: a header band with the logo, the name and a short description (drag it to move the window), every section (Who gets an arrow, Look, Preview, Party colours) in its own box, switches instead of check boxes, flat buttons, the addon's own tooltips and a thin outline on all texts.
- The key binding now shows a toast at the top of the screen ("Highlight: Off.") instead of a line in the chat. Click a toast to close it.
- The amber warning about dungeons and raids moved from under the title bar to the bottom of the editor.
- Reset next to each section title is now only an icon, without the word. The first click shows "Click again" in red.
- Party colours is a table with Name and Colour columns.
- The colour picker is called "Colour" and sits next to the editor at the height of the Party colours box.
- Shorter tooltips, for example on Also above your target.
- The code is split into smaller files; your settings are kept.

### Removed
- The Expressway font. The windows use the game's own fonts again.

### Added
- A Reset link next to each section title (who gets an arrow, look, party colours) that puts only that section back to its defaults. It asks for a second click to confirm.
- Own font (Expressway) for the editor, colour picker and settings panel.
- Own flat check boxes and a new close cross in the editor title bar.

### Changed
- Friendly nameplates are no longer turned on inside dungeons, raids and scenarios, where arrows above friendly players can't be shown anyway. Your own setting comes back there.
- Lines and borders are now exactly one pixel thick at every UI scale.

### Removed
- The Defaults and Close buttons at the bottom of the editor.
- Dragging the arrow above yourself; it now always sits at its fixed spot.

### Added
- `shell` (ShellCheck) and `smoke` checks. The `toc` check now also catches Lua files missing from the `.toc` and duplicate entries.

### Changed
- The editor title bar no longer shows the version number.
- CI runs every check as its own job, picked up automatically from `scripts/check/`.
- Tag releases run all checks before packaging and publishing.

### Added
- Arrow above party and raid members, drawn on their nameplates.
- Modes: Off, Party and Party + Raid. The arrow above yourself is a separate option.
- Arrow shapes: a filled or outline triangle, or one to three chevrons that can fade out or stay equally bright.
- Class colors by default, with a colour per player that is remembered by name and realm.
- Own colour picker with a colour field, a hue bar, a preset for every class and a hex field.
- Arrow size and lift above the name.
- Optional arrow above your current target, for units with a nameplate. This never changes your nameplate settings.
- Editor window opened with `/gh`: movable, with a live preview and changes that show in the game world immediately.
- Amber strip under the editor title bar that says arrows don't work above friendly players inside dungeons and raids.
- The arrow above yourself can be dragged into place while the editor is open.
- Key binding to turn the arrows off and back on to the previous mode.
- Settings panel under Options > AddOns with a button that opens the editor.
- Addon icon.
- CD workflow that packages tagged releases, creates a GitHub release and publishes to CurseForge (requires the `CF_API_TOKEN` and `CF_PROJECT_ID` secrets).
